# Verdict: unhealthy

The GRPO actor is not trained on the outcome advantages of the sequences that earned them. `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` group-normalizes correctly, then broadcasts one scrambled row across the batch. Held-out accuracy never recovers the base model, and the optimization traces show a policy that barely moves.

## Root cause

The live path is the legacy trainer (`trainer.use_v1: false` in the W&B config for `offline-run-20260926_105216-l7my3znq`). `algorithm.adv_estimator` is `grpo` with `norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: true`, so `RayPPOTrainer.compute_advantage` calls `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` in `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py`. The vectorized estimator, which does `scalars.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask`, is registered only for `grpo_vectorized` and is not used.

Group normalization itself is right. Scores are summed over tokens, grouped by `uid` (rollout `n: 8`), and whitened with the unbiased group standard deviation. For binary 0/1 outcomes that produces a known set of scalars: one success in eight is about `+2.47486673 / −0.35355239`; four of eight is about `±0.93541260`; a uniform group is 0. Every logged `critic/advantages/max` and `min` is one of those eight values (or 0). Step 283 is exactly `advantages/max = 2.4748666286468506` and `advantages/min = −0.935412585735321`.

The next lines throw that vector away as a per-sequence advantage. With batch size 128 and `max_response_length` 4096:

```python
row = scores.reshape(1, -1)          # (1, 128)
row = pad(row, to response_length)    # (1, 4096), tail zeros
scores = row.expand(bsz, -1) * response_mask
```

Every sequence receives the same prefix of the batch score vector, masked by its own response length. Sequence `i` does not get `scores[i]` on its tokens. `metric_utils` then takes a masked max/min over that tensor, so the logged extrema still show the raw group scalars. Those extrema are evidence that normalization ran, not that the actor was credited for the right samples.

The reward makes the misalignment decisive. `taco.compute_score` returns a binary all-tests-pass `score` (and the same value as `acc`). `NaiveRewardManager` writes that scalar only onto the last valid response token. Policy loss is token-mean PPO (`loss_agg_mode: token-mean`, clip 0.2, `ppo_epochs: 1`). The gradient at the reinforced token is therefore whatever foreign scalar landed at index `L-1`: `scores[L-1]` when `L <= 128`, else 0. A sequence carries its own advantage there only when its response length is `i+1`. On 2000 simulated batches of 128 (pass rate 0.12, lengths near the observed mean), that happens on about 0.11% of sequences. Mean absolute last-token advantage is about 0.06, against about 0.45 if each sequence kept its own scalar.

## Causal chain

1. Training reward is sparse and real. `critic/score/mean` window averages stay about 0.125 (steps 1–20), 0.115, 0.127, 0.133, 0.129, 0.122, then 0.093 (steps 251–284). `score/max` still hits 1. So some rollouts fully pass, and mixed groups of eight do produce the ±2.47 / ±0.94 advantages above.
2. Those advantages are not aligned to the passing sequences. Token-mean `actor/pg_loss` equals `-critic/advantages/mean` on all 280 logged update steps (difference under `1e-6`), and that mean stays near 0 (absolute mean about `3e-4`, largest absolute mean about 0.014). `actor/pg_clipfrac` and `actor/ppo_kl` are 0 on every update. Rollout-vs-train KL stays about `5e-4` and probability Pearson correlation about 0.9995 through step 284. Gradients stay finite (window means about 0.38 down to 0.18). There is no NaN, OOM, or traceback.
3. With `use_kl_loss: false`, `kl_loss_coef: 0`, `use_kl_in_reward: false`, and `entropy_coeff: 0`, nothing else anchors the policy. The only behavioral drift is longer, slightly higher-entropy samples under train temperature 1.0: response length about 174 → about 440, entropy about 0.47 → about 0.56. Response clip is 0 except five steps at `1/128`. Prompt clip is 0.
4. Held-out `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` (184 problems, `n: 1`, temperature 0.7, same binary `acc`) starts at 0.07609 (14/184) before training and is then 0.04891 (9), 0.05978 (11), 0.07065 (13), 0.04348 (8), and 0.05435 (10) at steps 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250. Every eval is below the base model; the best later eval is 13/184. `pass_rate` stays roughly flat (0.195 → peak 0.226 at step 150 → 0.195 at step 250) because it is not the optimized reward. Train binary reward does not rise either, so this is not a train/val metric mismatch.

## Symptoms, not causes

- The log stops at step 284 of `total_training_steps: 400` after a complete metric line. A later reprint of steps 211–212 is logger reorder. `save_freq` is 400, so no checkpoint is expected. Truncation did not create the flat loss or the earlier val drop.
- `timing_s/gen` is often ~120s (172/280 steps over 100s) because `compute_score/max` is ~121s on 171/280 steps while the mean score time is ~2s. Large TACO suites (held-out median ~200 tests, per-case alarm 4s, global cap 120s) slow the step. They do not zero the policy gradient.
- The launch script defaults to 8 GPUs; this host ran 4. That changes throughput only.
- Train problems have far fewer tests than the held-out set (median 5 vs ~200). That makes `pass_rate` look healthier than binary `acc`. It does not explain `pg_loss ≈ 0` while advantage extrema sit at the full group-normalized values.
- Logged TACO failures are a cap of two samples per step, mostly `result=False` wrong answers, not scorer exceptions. Val `n=1` on 184 items is noisy, but five consecutive evals below 14/184, together with a train reward that never trends up and a policy KL that never leaves ~1e-3, is failed learning.

The binary TACO reward sits only on the last response token, so the token-mean PPO update is weighted by some other sample’s scalar, or by zero.

Logged `advantages/max` and `min` still match the n=8 group formula exactly (step 283: `+2.4748666286468506` and `−0.935412585735321`), because those metrics reduce over the scrambled tensor. `pg_loss` equals the negative of `advantages/mean` on every update, both near zero; `pg_clipfrac` and `ppo_kl` stay 0; rollout–train KL stays about `5e-4`. Held-out accuracy starts at 14/184 and is 9, 11, 13, 8, and 10 at steps 50–250. The log ending at step 284 and the ~120s scoring stalls are symptoms, not the cause.
